 MADISON, Wis. -- JT Harms has been a reliable presence in net all season long for Forward Madison, and his efforts haven't gone unnoticed.
 Harms was named a finalist Friday for the USL League One Goalkeeper of the Year Award alongside Union Omaha's Cole Jensen and Charlotte Independence's Matt Levy.
 The 24-year-old from Whitefish Bay anchored a Mingos defense that was the only team in the league to allow less than a goal-per-game in 2026. He tallied 10 clean sheets, tied with former Mingo Bernd Schipmann for most in the league.
 Harms is up against stiff competition for the award. Jensen had the best save percentage in the league this season (78.3%), conceding only 15 goals across 17 matches started. Levy posted the second-best save percentage in the league (72.5%) and made 102 saves to help his team top the league table.
 While it is unlikely to sway the results, voters will get to see Harms and Levy go head-to-head on Sunday. Forward Madison travels to North Carolina to take on the Charlotte Independence in the USL League One Playoffs semifinals, with kickoff set for 6 p.m. CT.
